title: CLO 2025.1 - 2D
description: CLO 2025.1 new version fully upgraded to further enhance your work efficiency! In the new version, we have also optimized the 2D tools. Watch the video to learn about all the updates.
transcript:
This video introduces 2D function-related updates for everyone.  
In version 2025.0, we launched the AI version of the generator, which is used to create paper samples.  
Now, it has been further enhanced and can support the input of real images.  
Select the main menu bar 2D.  
Open the version generator.  
Select the clothing type according to the measurement values of the generated parameterized version.  
In addition, you can also use the AI version of the generator.  
It is located in the upper right corner of the generator.  
Click to open a new window.  
Here you can choose to enter a prompt to describe the clothing you want or upload a reference picture.  
From version 2025.1, you can choose to upload real images.  
Click to switch to image options.  
Click to upload the clothing you want.  
After uploading, click to start generation.  
CLO will automatically draw the paper sample according to the photos uploaded.  
You can preview it in the window of the 2D version.  
Once generation is complete, click to close.  
You can also continue to modify the measurement values in the version generator to get closer to the ideal effect.  
Finally, click to create.  
The paper sample will be placed in the 2D window.  
Now, the simple image will be converted into a custom version of the online store image you like.  
It becomes more intuitive and convenient, making the design process more relaxed.  

In version 2025.1, you can be more flexible.  
Define points as number points or non-number points.  
Number points follow the set numerical rules.  
Non-number points will smartly adapt to the movement of number points to maintain the exact proportion of the entire pattern.  
Use the Edit Number tool to select the actual point on the pattern to make it easier to identify.  
Now the number point edge will be displayed in green.  
Right-click on one of the number points.  
You can convert it to a non-number point.  
The non-number point will return to the standard appearance without green highlights.  
You can also select the frame or press the Shift key to choose multiple number points to convert.  
Non-number points will change according to the movement of number points.  
Of course, you can also convert the point back to a number point, so that when adjusting other points, the number point rule of this point is fixed.  
Similarly, if you use the Edit Curve Number tool,  
you can also change the number point.  
Then you can identify the number point of the curve point.  
You can convert the curve point to a number point or a non-number point.  
Through this update,  
users can control number points more accurately.  

In the previous version,  
the inner line on the symmetrical pattern could not be directly aligned to the symmetrical axis.  
You had to manually move the starting point of the line segment to the symmetrical axis.  
A new option has been added in version 2025.1.  
You can align the inner line to the symmetrical axis to make editing the pattern more convenient.  
Use the Edit Pattern tool.  
Right-click on one of the points near the symmetrical axis on the inner line.  
Select Align.  
Select the new option below: To Symmetrical Axis.  
The selected point will extend to the symmetrical axis at this time.  
The point on the other side remains unchanged.  
Then right-click on the point on the other side.  
You can choose to align it to the outside of the pattern.  
Extend the inner line to the outside of the pattern.  
In addition, you can also directly right-click on the inner line.  
Select Align to Symmetrical Axis.  
You will find that the two ends of the inner line at this time  
will be extended to the symmetrical axis and the outside of the pattern.  
This update makes editing the inner line of the symmetrical pattern  
more convenient and efficient.  

In the previous version,  
for use on symmetrical patterns,  
between lines,  
the inner line generated by the inner line function  
needed manual adjustment of the endpoint of the line to the symmetrical axis if you wanted it aligned.  
Now, a new option has been added.  
You can set the generated inner line  
to extend to the symmetrical axis of the pattern.  
Press Shift to select the middle line and the bottom curve at the same time.  
On the selected line,  
right-click and select Between Lines.  
The inner line generation window will open.  
You can see in the pop-up window  
a new option added at the bottom: Align to Symmetrical Axis.  
When this option is not enabled,  
the inner line behaves as before,  
extending to the outside of the pattern.  
When you enable the option to align to the symmetrical axis,  
the inner line will align to the symmetrical axis.  
Press Confirm to see the result.  
You can see the inner line generated on the selected side of the symmetrical pattern.  
The other side will also be generated simultaneously,  
and the two inner lines are based on the symmetrical axis.  
Now in version 2025.1,  
users can make more flexible decisions  
based on the extension of the inner line generated between two lines.  

In version 2025.1,  
you can now set the default cutout type and length  
to meet your specific requirements.  
Find the main menu bar.  
Set User Default 2D.  
Here you can set the cutout display,  
fixed screen length or actual length,  
and select your preferred cutout type  
as default options.  
Select the display type Fixed Screen Length.  
Then select cutout type V.  
Use the cutout tool to add a cutout.  
Use the cutout tool to add a cutout.  
Use the cutout tool to add a cutout.  
Note that when selecting Fixed Screen Length,  
the length will be adjusted by adjusting the screen,  
and the length set in the property editor is not editable.  
Open the default window again.  
If you select Actual Length,  
it means that the cutout length is fixed to the set value.  
Enter the actual length 5mm. Set the cutout type I.  
Use the cutout tool to select the cutout to be added.  
You can modify the length in the property editor.  
By setting the default cutout type and length update,  
users do not need to manually adjust the size and type of the cutout.  
We hope this update can help you use cutouts more conveniently.

chunks.content: ## 2D Generator Enhancements in CLO 2025.1 This section covers the improvements to the 2D version generator in CLO 2025.1, focusing on AI-powered image input, paper sample creation, and workflow enhancements for clothing design. In version 2025.0, CLO introduced an AI-based generator for creating paper samples. Version 2025.1 further enhances this feature by allowing users to input real images directly into the AI generator. To use this: - Select the main menu bar and open the 2D version generator. - Choose the clothing type based on measurement values from the parameterized version. - In the upper right corner of the generator, open the AI version generator. - Enter a descriptive prompt or switch to the image upload option. - Upload a reference photo of the clothing design. - Click "Start Generation" to have CLO automatically create the paper sample based on the uploaded image. - Preview the generated sample in the 2D version window. - Adjust measurement values in the version generator if needed to refine the design. - Click "Create" to place the final paper sample into the 2D window. This update makes it easier and more intuitive to transform simple images into customized, parameterized clothing patterns, streamlining the design process. --- ## Flexible Number Point and Curve Point Control This section explains how CLO 2025.1 improves control over pattern points, distinguishing between number points and non-number points for precise pattern adjustments. Version 2025.1 introduces the ability to define points as either number points or non-number points: - **Number points** adhere to fixed numerical rules and maintain pattern proportions rigidly. - **Non-number points** adapt dynamically to movements of number points to preserve overall pattern proportion. Using the **Edit Number Tool**: - Select a point on the pattern; number points are highlighted with green edges. - Right-click a number point to convert it to a non-number point, which loses the green highlight. - Multiple points can be selected (using Shift) for bulk conversion. - Non-number points move relative to number points but do not follow fixed numerical constraints. - Points can be converted back to number points to fix their adjustment rules. Similarly, the **Edit Curve Number Tool** allows number and non-number classification of curve points, enhancing accurate control of curved pattern sections. This update enables users to manage pattern points more precisely, balancing fixed measurements with flexible adaptations. --- ## Symmetrical Pattern Inner Line Alignment This section details new options for aligning inner lines on symmetrical patterns to improve editing efficiency and accuracy. Previously, inner lines on symmetrical patterns could not be automatically aligned to the symmetrical axis; manual adjustment of line endpoints was required. In version 2025.1, new alignment options include: - Using the **Edit Pattern Tool**, right-click a point near the symmetrical axis on the inner line. - Select **Align > To Symmetrical Axis** to extend that point directly to the axis; the opposite point remains unchanged. - Right-click the opposite point to choose **Align to Outside of Pattern**, extending the inner line outward.

chunks.title: CLO 2025.1 - 2D
chunks.content: Previously, inner lines on symmetrical patterns could not be automatically aligned to the symmetrical axis; manual adjustment of line endpoints was required. In version 2025.1, new alignment options include: - Using the **Edit Pattern Tool**, right-click a point near the symmetrical axis on the inner line. - Select **Align > To Symmetrical Axis** to extend that point directly to the axis; the opposite point remains unchanged. - Right-click the opposite point to choose **Align to Outside of Pattern**, extending the inner line outward. - Alternatively, right-click the inner line itself and select **Align to Symmetrical Axis** to simultaneously extend both ends—the inner end to the symmetrical axis and the outer end beyond the pattern edge. These features simplify symmetrical pattern editing by automating inner line alignment and reducing manual endpoint adjustments. --- ## Inner Line Generation Between Lines with Symmetrical Axis Alignment This section explains the improved inner line generation function between lines, adding symmetrical axis alignment for automatic pattern consistency. Previously, inner lines generated between symmetrical pattern lines required manual endpoint adjustment to align with the symmetrical axis. Version 2025.1 introduces a new option in the **Between Lines** inner line generation window: - Select two lines (e.g., middle line and bottom curve) by pressing Shift. - Right-click and choose **Between Lines** to open the inner line generation dialog. - At the bottom, a new checkbox option: **Align to Symmetrical Axis**. - When unchecked, inner lines extend outside the pattern as before. - When enabled, inner lines align precisely to the symmetrical axis. - Confirm to generate inner lines; both sides of the symmetrical pattern are updated simultaneously based on the axis. This update provides users with more flexible control over inner line placement on symmetrical patterns, improving design accuracy and workflow efficiency. --- ## Default Cutout Type and Length Settings This section covers the new ability to set default cutout types and lengths in CLO 2025.1, streamlining cutout management in 2D pattern design. Users can now configure default cutout display and dimensions via: - Main menu bar > **Set User Default 2D**. - Options to set cutout display mode: **Fixed Screen Length** or **Actual Length**. - Selection of preferred default cutout type (e.g., V-cut, I-cut). Details: - **Fixed Screen Length** mode adjusts cutout length visually based on screen scaling; the length property in the editor is non-editable in this mode. - **Actual Length** mode fixes the cutout length to a specific measurement (e.g., 5mm), allowing length modification via the property editor. Using the cutout tool with these defaults: - Adds cutouts of the predefined type and length automatically. - Eliminates the need for manual size and type adjustments on each cutout. This feature enhances consistency and convenience in applying cutouts during 2D pattern editing.
